newsitem.title: UK: Crest completes FTSE 100 share transition.
newsitem.headline: Crest completes FTSE 100 share transition.

text.p: CRESTCo, the Bank of England-led group that runs the computerised share settlement system for the London Stock Exchange (LSE), said on Monday it has transferred all 100 FTSE stocks to its new system, Crest.
The move ends an era of paper-based settlements for Britain's biggest blue chip shares.
Crest replaces the LSE's 18-year-old paper-based system, Talisman, which will close on Friday, the exchange said.
CRESTCo, a consortium of 60 financial institutions which came together to build the new system after the LSE's own attempt to develop a computerised system failed, launched Crest in July last year.
FTSE 100 stocks gradually were moved into the electronic settlement regime.
The group met its target date to complete the transfer despite initial software glitches that led to huge backlogs and other problems late last year.
CRESTCo has bolstered the capacity of Crest by 60 percent so that it could deal with the onslaught of paper from building societies later this year.

Various user fees will be introduced to cover the costs of the additional computer capacity. CRESTCo said it has not yet decided when the new fee structure will be introduced. --Debra Sherman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
